title: Decision-tree admission controller for fallback-mode selection
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement an admission controller that uses a decision-tree policy to pick a per-request fallback or degradation mode. The controller must consult per-tenant SLOs, current region health, model-cost estimates, remaining token budgets, KV-cache signals, and request deadlines to choose from a set of actions: accept, accept-with-trim, degrade-to-slim-model, serve-from-cache, queue-with-timeout, or soft-reject with friendly client error. Goal: keep P95 latency and error-rate SLOs stable during regional capacity loss or spikes while minimizing quality regressions and customer-visible rejections.
acceptance_criteria: Decision-tree policy implemented as a configurable component behind the global admission API
Per-tenant credit ledger with decay/hysteresis published to metrics and used for soft admission
Controller chooses degradation mode in >= 99% of simulated spike traces and reduces hard rejects by >= 45% compared to baseline
End-to-end canary in two regions with canary traffic showing P95 within 1.2x of steady-state for 95% of requests
Comprehensive playbook for on-call that maps signals to operator actions (circuit trip, rollback, manual reroute)
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike-simulation harness created (github.com/redwood-inference/sim/issue/347201) and initial traces imported from last incident
2026-03-04: Prototype decision tree v0 implemented in alpha admission service; uses tenant_weight, sla_tier, kv_cache_hit, region_health_score, token_budget_remaining, estimated_model_cost
2026-03-06: Benchmarked prototype: reduces hard reject rate by 38% but increases median tail trimming operations; flagged trade-off with per-request trimming complexity
2026-03-08: Design review with PM and Design; agreed to surface degradation reason codes in response headers for client observability; PR #7123 opened for telemetry work
2026-03-10: Implemented per-tenant credit decay (half-life 10m) and hysteresis to avoid oscillation; integration tests added
decisions: Use a deterministic decision tree (config-driven) rather than ML policy for first rollout to simplify auditing and allow human-readable fallbacks
Expose canonical 'degradation_reason' and 'chosen_fallback' fields on response header and Console logs
Keep soft-reject (429 with retry-after + reason) for tenants that exhaust credits to preserve fair share
Token-budgeting: implement token-decay ledger (time-decayed credits) instead of hard daily budgets to allow burst absorbtion
Circuit breaker per-region will be quorum-aware: require 2/3 infra signals (latency QPS, instance health, model-pool saturation) to flip to forced-fallback mode
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Trimming content causes unacceptable hallucination regressions for some customers; Mitigation: provide per-tenant fidelity profiles and opt-out capability
Risk: Decision tree thresholds cause oscillation under borderline load; Mitigation: hysteresis and credit half-life plus smoothing metrics (30s rolling windows)
Risk: Increased operational complexity for on-call; Mitigation: add automated runbook triggers and a concise playbook card in Console with one-click reroute to backup region
test_plan: Unit tests for decision branches and telemetry emissions
Integration tests with kv-cache stub to validate serve-from-cache branch
Chaos tests: induce 30%-50% model-pool saturation and validate controller chooses degradations without hard rejects
Canary rollout: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% in two non-primary regions with synthetic and real replayed traffic
Quality eval: run prompt set A/B to measure content quality delta for 'trim' and 'slim-model' modes; require <8% quality regression for P1 tenants
rollout_plan: Week 1: Internal alpha traffic in staging, iterate thresholds
Week 2: Canary to 1% production in secondary region, monitor slo_metrics and fidelity_metrics
Week 3: Expand to 10% with rollback watch windows and on-call ready
Week 4: Full rollout region-by-region, enable per-tenant opt-out controls in Console
operator_playbook: Signal: p95 latency > 1.5x and hard rejects > 1% for 5 minutes => Action: verify region_health_score and circuit state; if region_circuit open then enable forced-degrade mode and escalate
Signal: sudden increase in 'trim' ratio and fidelity alerts => Action: reduce trimming aggressiveness config and open rollback PR to revert tree thresholds
Signal: per-tenant complaints for hallucinations => Action: run fidelity eval job for tenant, optionally pin them to higher-fidelity model or disable trimming for that tenant

Emergency: region health unknown / control plane degraded => Action: reroute ingress to alternate region via edge-routing toggle (Console one-click), enable global soft-admission with conservative thresholds
notes: Novelty: combining token-decay credits with a deterministic, auditable decision tree gives a predictable operator surface compared to opaque ML policies
We will instrument a 'fallback-cost-savings' metric to quantify economic impact of each chosen fallback mode and feed into Optimize recommendations
Follow-up: explore an ML ranker that selects the minimal-quality-impact fallback for each request after deterministic policy proves safe
